# THEORYs with `tags` `social-identity`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds whatever reading the owner files here, whether or not an Anthology of the SOTA topic could also hold it; instruction for ML practice belongs to the anthology (ADR-048). The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Social identity** — the psychology of group membership — social identity and self-categorization theory, how people categorize themselves and others and when a group identity becomes salient, identification and its measurement, in-group bias and intergroup relations, rivalry, recategorization and common in-group identity, group-based emotion, crowds and fandom. What a group is, as ontology, is social-ontology; here it is how people come to see themselves and act as members (ADR-062).

| [THEORY-1111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1111.md) | Commodification shifts fans to flâneurs | Giulianotti (2002), [LIT-1150](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1150.md), read from the author's pre-review text. Four ideal types: supporters (traditional/hot: kin-like, topophilic, obligatory), followers (traditional/cool: nested, mediated allegiances), fans (consumer/hot: non-reciprocal intimacy, authenticated by consumption) and flâneurs (consumer/cool: cosmopolitan window-shoppers of clubs). Hypercommodification is said to move identification from supporter towards flâneur, while the spectacle flâneurs consume depends on supporters. Proposed: a conceptual classification with no data, and a trend claim that is asserted, not measured. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1112](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1112.md) | Groupness needs inferred collective intention | Skorich (2025, v2 2026), [LIT-1765](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1765.md), a preprint. Categorization with accentuation makes members interchangeable, not one, since a category is a set and a set is internally differentiated. Groups such as orchestras and families need no similarity. Groups are holistic entities perceived from cues to shared mental states, much as faces are perceived from configuration. Reported support: four experiments under review in which groups defined by a mental state (a chosen T-shirt colour; seeing the duck or the rabbit) drew more favouritism and tracking than groups defined by a physical property. Proposed: the argument is conceptual and the evidence is unpublished. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-1114](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1114.md) v3 | Metacontrast sets salient self-categories | Self-categorization theory as restated by Turner, Oakes, Haslam and McGarty (1994), [LIT-1794](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1794.md), and reviewed by Hornsey (2008), [LIT-1742](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1742.md). Personal and social identity are levels of self-categorization. Salience is perceiver readiness times fit, comparative fit being the metacontrast ratio. The level, kind, content and prototype structure of self-categories shift with the comparison set: Americans read as less aggressive beside Iraq than beside the Soviet Union, and a group's extreme members become more prototypical in an intergroup context. Proposed: every result in the record comes through the theory's authors, reported without data, and the account's stronger claim, that the self is generated rather than stored, is not part of it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1115](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1115.md) v2 | We-identity needs no depersonalization | León (2023), [LIT-1721](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1721.md). Self-categorization theory claims depersonalization as "the basic process underlying group phenomena", for groups of any size, friendship groups included (Turner et al. 1987, pp. 50, 103, as quoted), and phenomenologists have taken it as the account of the "we". But close relationships yield we-identities while their members grasp each other as non-substitutable, and relationship research on couple resilience finds the "we" more adaptive the more differentiated the "I". Proposed: the argument is conceptual, and the cited evidence was not analysed by the source or read here. | Proposed |
